content:
The triangle inequalities all hold, since
\[
13+17=30>12\sqrt2,\quad 13+12\sqrt2>17,\quad 17+12\sqrt2>13.
\]
Using Heron’s formula with semiperimeter
\[
s=\frac{13+17+12\sqrt2}{2}=15+6\sqrt2,
\]
\[
A^2=s(s-13)(s-17)(s-12\sqrt2)
\]
\[
=(15+6\sqrt2)(2+6\sqrt2)(-2+6\sqrt2)(15-6\sqrt2).
\]
Pairing terms:
\[
(15+6\sqrt2)(15-6\sqrt2)=153,
\]
\[
(2+6\sqrt2)(-2+6\sqrt2)=68.
\]
Thus
\[
A^2=153\cdot 68=10404,
\]
so
\[
A=102.
\]

\boxed{102}
